If they are predicating the second meaning, they are making a common-sense description of a human fetus that cannot be denied. Predicating this second meaning now requires the pro-life advocate to prove whether that life of the human variety is in fact a distinct human being. Even before that, the argument fails from the first premise — Humans don’t have rights.

Read the language of the Constitution, or any other document that describes the rights afforded to an individual. It doesn’t use the word “Human”. It uses the word “Person” or “People”.

Now, “Person” is a subcategory of “Human”. But it is a specific category that includes living, independent Human Beings in totality with sentience and sapience (that is not the exact definition, just paraphrasing as an example). But, for example, let’s even take away the “part of a human vs the whole thing” confusion — look at a corpse. That is not a part of a Human, that is, taxonomically, a Human Being. There is no other word to describe it other than “Human”. But it is not a “Person”, and does not have rights, at least not the same rights that we afford to People. For example, if you were to bury a Person, or cremate them, or cut them open on an operating table without their medical consent and root around in their organs, that would clearly be violating their rights… but a cadaver is a Human, not a Person, so doesn’t have those rights.
